claim: Repulsive bias and minimum variance observed near cardinal axes are well-known error patterns typically associated with visual orientation perception.
source: Repulsive bias and minimum variance observed near cardinal axes are well-known error patterns typically associated with visual orientation perception.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field of visual orientation perception.

claim: Recent experiments suggest that errors in visual working memory continuously evolve during working memory.
source: Recent experiments suggest that these errors continuously evolve during working memory, posing a challenge that neither static sensory models nor traditional memory models can address.
evidence: The claim references recent experimental findings without specific citations in this sentence.

claim: Evolving errors with characteristic shapes require network interaction between two distinct modules.
source: Here, we demonstrate that these evolving errors, maintaining characteristic shapes, require network interaction between two distinct modules.
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated through the modeling work presented in the manuscript.

claim: Each module fulfills efficient sensory encoding and memory maintenance, which cannot be achieved simultaneously in a single-module network.
source: Each module fulfills efficient sensory encoding and memory maintenance, which cannot be achieved simultaneously in a single-module network.
evidence: This is a key finding from the comparative analysis of single-module versus two-module networks presented in the manuscript.

claim: The sensory module exhibits heterogeneous tuning with strong inhibitory modulation reflecting natural orientation statistics.
source: The sensory module exhibits heterogeneous tuning with strong inhibitory modulation reflecting natural orientation statistics.
evidence: This is a design feature of the model demonstrated through network simulations and analysis.

claim: The memory module, operating alone, supports homogeneous representation via continuous attractor dynamics.
source: While the memory module, operating alone, supports homogeneous representation via continuous attractor dynamics, the fully connected network forms discrete attractors with moderate drift speed and nonuniform diffusion processes.
evidence: This is demonstrated through network simulations showing the properties of the isolated memory module.

claim: The fully connected network forms discrete attractors with moderate drift speed and nonuniform diffusion processes.
source: While the memory module, operating alone, supports homogeneous representation via continuous attractor dynamics, the fully connected network forms discrete attractors with moderate drift speed and nonuniform diffusion processes.
evidence: This is demonstrated through low-dimensional analysis of the two-module network dynamics.

claim: Biases of errors observed in estimation tasks have been used as indirect evidence to infer changes in the internal representations of stimuli.
source: For instance, biases of errors, the systematic deviation from the original stimuli, observed in estimation tasks have been used as indirect evidence to infer changes in the internal representations of stimuli (Wei and Stocker, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wei and Stocker, 2017.

claim: Cardinal repulsion refers to the systematic shift away from the horizontal and vertical orientations observed in many perceptual tasks.
source: Cardinal repulsion, which refers to the systematic shift away from the horizontal and vertical orientations observed in many perceptual tasks, is one of the examples (de Gardelle et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to de Gardelle et al., 2010.

claim: Cardinal repulsion reflects the prevalence of the cardinal orientations in natural scenes.
source: Theoretical works suggest that such a bias pattern reflects the prevalence of the cardinal orientations in natural scenes (Girshick et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Girshick et al., 2011.

claim: The variance of errors for orientation stimuli was found to be inversely proportional to the stimulus statistics, minimum at cardinal and maximum at oblique orientations.
source: Similarly, the variance of errors for orientation stimuli was found to be inversely proportional to the stimulus statistics, minimum at cardinal and maximum at oblique orientations (van Bergen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to van Bergen et al., 2015.

claim: The dependence of biases and variance of errors on natural statistics results from sensory encoding optimized to enhance precision around the most common stimuli.
source: It was postulated that the dependence of biases and variance of errors on natural statistics results from sensory encoding optimized to enhance precision around the most common stimuli (Ganguli and Simoncelli, 2014; Wei and Stocker, 2015; Wei and Stocker, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ganguli and Simoncelli, 2014; Wei and Stocker, 2015; Wei and Stocker, 2017.

claim: Representations of orientation or color stimuli undergo gradual and continuous modifications throughout the delay period in delayed estimation tasks.
source: In delayed estimation tasks, where participants are presented with stimuli followed by a delay period during which they rely on their working memory for estimation, it has been observed that representations of orientation or color stimuli undergo gradual and continuous modifications throughout the delay period (Panichello et al., 2019; Bae, 2021; Gu et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Panichello et al., 2019; Bae, 2021; Gu et al., 2023.

claim: Dynamic error patterns are inconsistent with sensory encoding models, most of which only establish a static relationship between stimuli and internal representations.
source: Such dynamic error patterns are inconsistent with sensory encoding models, most of which only establish a static relationship between stimuli and internal representations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations of existing sensory encoding models.

claim: Traditional working memory models are constructed to faithfully maintain information about stimuli during the delay period.
source: Most of them are constructed to faithfully maintain information about stimuli during the delay period, and thus, the memory representation has a similar geometry as that of the stimuli (Wang, 2001; Khona and Fiete, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wang, 2001; Khona and Fiete, 2022.

claim: For continuous stimuli such as orientation, all stimuli are equally maintained in ring-like memory activities in traditional memory models, predicting no biases.
source: For continuous stimuli such as orientation, location, direction, or color, all stimuli are equally maintained in ring-like memory activities, predicting no biases (Zhang, 1996; Compte et al., 2000; Burak and Fiete, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zhang, 1996; Compte et al., 2000; Burak and Fiete, 2009.

claim: Cardinal orientations are the most prevalent in natural images.
source: In natural images, cardinal orientations are the most prevalent (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Error patterns in estimation tasks show dependence on natural statistics, such as biases away from cardinal orientations where the variance of errors is nonetheless minimal.
source: Error patterns in estimation tasks show dependence on such natural statistics, such as biases away from cardinal orientations where the variance of errors is nonetheless minimal (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figures 1B and C.

claim: In delayed estimation tasks, bias patterns are consolidated in time.
source: In delayed estimation tasks, such a bias pattern is consolidated in time (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Estimation errors increase with a longer delay in delayed estimation tasks.
source: Also, experimental data suggested that estimation errors increase with a longer delay (Wimmer et al., 2014; Schneegans and Bays, 2018), while the precision is still highest at cardinal orientations (van den Berg et al., 2012; Bays, 2014; van Bergen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wimmer et al., 2014; Schneegans and Bays, 2018; van den Berg et al., 2012; Bays, 2014; van Bergen et al., 2015.

claim: Continuous attractor models assume that all orientations are equally encoded and maintained.
source: The most widely accepted model for working memory of orientation stimuli has continuous attractor dynamics, which assumes that all orientations are equally encoded and maintained (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1D-F.

claim: In continuous attractor models, without external input, there is no systematic shift of mean activity during the delay period.
source: Without external input, there is no systematic shift of mean activity, i.e., no drift during the delay period (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1E.

claim: In continuous attractor models with constant noise, the variance of errors is spatially flat with constant diffusion along the ring.
source: Also, under the assumption of equal influence of noise for all orientations, the variance of errors is spatially flat with constant diffusion along the ring, while the overall magnitude increases over time due to the accumulation of noise (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1F.

claim: Discrete attractor models with constant noise yield inconsistent results when inferring the locus of attractors from the bias and variance patterns observed in the data.
source: However, discrete attractor models with constant noise yield inconsistent results when inferring the locus of attractors from the bias and variance patterns observed in the data.
evidence: This is an inference from the analysis of discrete attractor models presented in the manuscript.

claim: Discrete attractors with maximum noise at the obliques could reproduce experimentally observed error patterns of orientation stimuli.
source: In sum, unlike two prominent memory models, continuous attractors or discrete attractors with constant noise, discrete attractors with maximum noise at the obliques could reproduce experimentally observed error patterns of orientation stimuli.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the low-dimensional attractor model analysis.

claim: Bayesian inference with efficient coding could generate the repulsive bias and the lowest variance at cardinal orientations.
source: Before exploring full memory network models, we note that previous theoretical works for sensory processing suggested that Bayesian inference with efficient coding could generate the repulsive bias and the lowest variance at cardinal orientations (Wei and Stocker, 2015; Wei and Stocker, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wei and Stocker, 2015; Wei and Stocker, 2017.

claim: Efficient coding theory suggests the sensory system should enhance the sensitivity around more common stimuli.
source: Efficient coding theory suggests the sensory system should enhance the sensitivity around more common stimuli.
evidence: This is a statement of efficient coding theory.

claim: For orientation stimuli, precision should be highest around cardinal directions, which could be achieved by sharpening the likelihood functions.
source: For orientation stimuli, precision should be highest around cardinal directions, which could be achieved by sharpening the likelihood functions.
evidence: This is an application of efficient coding theory to orientation stimuli.

claim: Recurrent interaction between sensory and memory systems during the delay period successfully reproduces correct error patterns observed in memory tasks.
source: Thus, recurrent interaction between sensory and memory systems during the delay period, each of which meets different demands, successfully reproduces correct error patterns observed in memory tasks.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the extended Bayesian model analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: The connectivity strengths across columns in the sensory module are heterogeneous, particularly stronger at the obliques.
source: Furthermore, the connectivity strengths across columns are heterogeneous, particularly stronger at the obliques.
evidence: This is a design feature of the sensory module in the network model.

claim: The tuning curves near cardinal orientations can be sharper and denser in the sensory module.
source: As a result, the tuning curves near cardinal orientations can be sharper and denser, consistent with experimental observations showing a larger number of cardinally tuned neurons (Li et al., 2003; Shen et al., 2014) and their narrower tuning (Li et al., 2003; Kreile et al., 2011; Figure 3C–F, left).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li et al., 2003; Shen et al., 2014; Kreile et al., 2011 and illustrated in Figure 3C-F.

claim: Experimental observations show a larger number of cardinally tuned neurons.
source: As a result, the tuning curves near cardinal orientations can be sharper and denser, consistent with experimental observations showing a larger number of cardinally tuned neurons (Li et al., 2003; Shen et al., 2014) and their narrower tuning (Li et al., 2003; Kreile et al., 2011; Figure 3C–F, left).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li et al., 2003; Shen et al., 2014.

claim: Cardinally tuned neurons have narrower tuning according to experimental observations.
source: As a result, the tuning curves near cardinal orientations can be sharper and denser, consistent with experimental observations showing a larger number of cardinally tuned neurons (Li et al., 2003; Shen et al., 2014) and their narrower tuning (Li et al., 2003; Kreile et al., 2011; Figure 3C–F, left).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li et al., 2003; Kreile et al., 2011.

claim: The sensory-memory interacting network exhibits repulsive bias and minimum variance at cardinal orientations.
source: When the internal representation of the orientation stimulus is read from the memory module using a population vector decoder mimicking Bayesian optimal readout (Fischer, 2010), the sensory-memory interacting network exhibits repulsive bias and minimum variance at cardinal orientations, inheriting from efficient sensory coding (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through network simulations and shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Fisher information is highest at cardinal orientations in the sensory-memory interacting network.
source: Opposite to the variance of errors, Fisher information is highest at cardinal orientations, while it decreases during the delay period (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through network simulations and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The network implements discrete attractor dynamics with attractors formed at the obliques.
source: This suggests that the network implements discrete attractor dynamics with attractors formed at the obliques.
evidence: This is inferred from the low-dimensional analysis of network dynamics.

claim: The diffusion term is uneven with maximum noise amplitude at the obliques.
source: The diffusion term is also uneven – the noise amplitude is maximum at the obliques so that despite attraction toward them, the variance of errors can be maximum (Figure 5C and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated through low-dimensional analysis and shown in Figure 5C and F.

claim: The nonuniform characteristics of both drift and diffusion processes stem from the heterogeneous connections within the sensory module.
source: Thus, the nonuniform characteristics of both drift and diffusion processes stem from the heterogeneous connections within the sensory module and align with the solution identified in low-dimensional memory models (Figure 1J–L).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analysis of network dynamics.

claim: Inhibitory synaptic connections can be modified through learning.
source: Inhibitory synaptic connections can also be modified through learning (Vogels et al., 2013; Khan et al., 2018; Larisch et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Vogels et al., 2013; Khan et al., 2018; Larisch et al., 2021.

claim: Stronger inhibitory modulation is required for correct bias and variance patterns.
source: Reversely, for relatively larger β with stronger modulation in inhibitory connections, the network reproduced cardinal repulsion and minimum variance of errors at cardinal orientations, consistent with experiments (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is demonstrated through network simulations with varying inhibitory modulation and shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Heterogeneously tuned inhibition plays an important role in shaping the sensory response for higher precision at cardinal orientations.
source: Thus, this emphasizes the important role of heterogeneously tuned inhibition in shaping the sensory response for higher precision at cardinal orientations and enabling the sensory-memory interacting network to generate correct error patterns.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analysis of excitatory and inhibitory modulation.

claim: Memory circuits with heterogeneous connections have problems in maintaining the information and reproducing correct error patterns.
source: However, memory circuits with heterogeneous connections have problems in maintaining the information and reproducing correct error patterns (Figure 8C–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through simulations of one-module networks and shown in Figure 8C-E.

claim: Memory circuits alone require fine-tuning of heterogeneity whose range generating a moderate drift speed is at least one order of magnitude smaller than that of the two-module network.
source: First, memory circuits alone require fine-tuning of heterogeneity whose range generating a moderate drift speed is at least one order of magnitude smaller than that of the two-module network (Figure 8C and D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through parameter analysis and shown in Figure 8C and D.

claim: In the one-module network, the variance pattern is reversed such that the variance of errors is minimal at the oblique orientations.
source: Second, despite the correct bias direction, the variance pattern is reversed such that the variance of errors is minimal at the oblique orientations (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through simulations and shown in Figure 8E.

claim: Interactions between heterogeneous sensory and homogeneous memory modules are advantageous due to an additional degree of freedom, intermodal connectivity strengths.
source: In sum, compared to a heterogeneous memory circuit alone, interactions between heterogeneous sensory and homogeneous memory modules are advantageous due to an additional degree of freedom, intermodal connectivity strengths, which allows better control of energy and noise difference at cardinal and oblique orientations.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the comparative analysis of one-module and two-module networks.

claim: Recent human studies found memory signals in early sensory areas.
source: While higher association areas have long been considered as a locus of working memory (Roussy et al., 2021; Mejías and Wang, 2022), recent human studies found memory signals in early sensory areas, prompting a re-evaluation of their role in working memory (Xu, 2020; Adam et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Xu, 2020; Adam et al., 2022.

claim: Efficient encoding necessitates asymmetrical connections, resulting in inconsistent bias and variance patterns and overly rapid drift in the one-module network unless fine-tuned.
source: Efficient encoding necessitates asymmetrical connections, resulting in inconsistent bias and variance patterns and overly rapid drift in the one-module network unless fine-tuned.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analysis of one-module networks.

claim: Connecting sensory and memory modules can generate error patterns correctly and with less need for fine-tuning heterogeneity for slow drift.
source: In contrast, connecting sensory and memory modules can generate error patterns correctly and with less need for fine-tuning heterogeneity for slow drift.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the comparative analysis of one-module and two-module networks.

claim: During the delay period, TMS can intervene with the feedforward signal from sensory areas through which working memory is consolidated.
source: Many studies have found that during the delay period, TMS can intervene with the feedforward signal from sensory areas through which working memory is consolidated (van de Ven et al., 2012) (but see Adam et al., 2022, for mixed effects of TMS and related debate).
evidence: This is supported by citations to van de Ven et al., 2012 and Adam et al., 2022.

claim: In the two-module network, perturbation will cause the bias to stop systematically drifting toward the obliques, reducing systematic repulsion.
source: However, we expect different effects on bias patterns — in the two-module network, the bias will stop systematically drifting toward the obliques, reducing systematic repulsion (Figure 10).
evidence: This is a prediction from the model shown in Figure 10.

claim: In the one-module network, perturbation does not incur changes in error patterns as memory activities are less dependent on the sensory module during the delay period.
source: In contrast, in the one-module network, perturbation does not incur changes in error patterns as memory activities are less dependent on the sensory module during the delay period.
evidence: This is a prediction from the model analysis.

claim: The model cannot predict the effects of distractors during working memory, as such effects do not experimentally lead to changes in error patterns.
source: Note that our model cannot predict the effects of distractors during working memory, as such effects do not experimentally lead to changes in error patterns (Rademaker et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a limitation of the model supported by a citation to Rademaker et al., 2019.

claim: The work narrows the mechanism to denser and narrower tuning curves at cardinal orientations, consistent with neurophysiological recordings in the visual cortex.
source: Our work narrowed the mechanism to denser and narrower tuning curves at cardinal orientations, consistent with neurophysiological recordings in the visual cortex (Li et al., 2003; Kreile et al., 2011; Shen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li et al., 2003; Kreile et al., 2011; Shen et al., 2014.

claim: A population vector decoder reflecting neuronal preferred orientations approximates Bayesian optimal readout.
source: We implemented a population vector decoder reflecting neuronal preferred orientations, which approximates Bayesian optimal readout (Fischer, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fischer, 2010.

claim: Recent work combined dynamic change of signal amplitude with static tuning curves to capture different time courses of estimation precision during sensory encoding and memory maintenance.
source: Notably, recent work combined dynamic change of signal amplitude with static tuning curves to capture different time courses of estimation precision during sensory encoding and memory maintenance (Tomić and Bays, 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tomić and Bays, 2023.

claim: Behavior studies showed attractive bias and minimum variance around the prevalent colors.
source: Behavior studies showed attractive bias and minimum variance around the prevalent colors, which one-module discrete attractor models could reproduce.
evidence: This is a statement about previous behavior studies on color memory.

claim: One-module discrete attractor models cannot be generalized to other visual stimuli, such as orientations, spatial locations, or directions, of which the responses show repulsive bias away from the common stimuli.
source: However, these models cannot be generalized to other visual stimuli, such as orientations, spatial locations, or directions, of which the responses show repulsive bias away from the common stimuli (Wei and Stocker, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wei and Stocker, 2017.

claim: A one-module network storing color memory requires fine-tuned heterogeneity for moderate drift speed.
source: Also, a one-module network storing color memory requires fine-tuned heterogeneity for moderate drift speed.
evidence: This is an inference from the analysis of one-module networks.

claim: Fine-tuning of homogeneous connections in the memory module can be mediated through activity-dependent plasticity, such as short-term facilitation or long-term plasticity.
source: Fine-tuning of homogeneous connections in the memory module can be mediated through activity-dependent plasticity, such as short-term facilitation (Itskov et al., 2011; Hansel and Mato, 2013; Seeholzer et al., 2019) or long-term plasticity (Renart et al., 2003; Gu and Lim, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Itskov et al., 2011; Hansel and Mato, 2013; Seeholzer et al., 2019; Renart et al., 2003; Gu and Lim, 2022.

claim: Continuous attractors formed under unstructured, heterogeneous connections are robust against synaptic perturbations.
source: Also, recent work showed that continuous attractors formed under unstructured, heterogeneous connections are robust against synaptic perturbations (Darshan and Rivkind, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Darshan and Rivkind, 2022.

claim: While shorter stimulus presentations with no explicit delay led to larger biases experimentally, the current model shows an increase in bias throughout the stimulus presentation.
source: For instance, while shorter stimulus presentations with no explicit delay led to larger biases experimentally, our current model, which starts activities from a flat baseline, shows an increase in bias throughout the stimulus presentation (de Gardelle et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a limitation of the model supported by a citation to de Gardelle et al., 2010.

claim: The error variance during stimulus presentation is almost negligible compared to that during the delay period in the model.
source: Additionally, the error variance during stimulus presentation is almost negligible compared to that during the delay period, as the external input overwhelms the internal noise.
evidence: This is an observation from the model simulations.

claim: A recent Bayesian perception model suggested different types of noise like external noise or variations in loss functions that adjust tolerance to small errors may help explain various error patterns observed across different modalities.
source: Also, a recent Bayesian perception model suggested different types of noise like external noise or variations in loss functions that adjust tolerance to small errors may help explain various error patterns observed across different modalities (Hahn and Wei, 2024).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hahn and Wei, 2024.

claim: For memories involving multiple items, noise can be critical in determining error patterns, as encoding more items might cause higher noise for each individual item.
source: Even for memories involving multiple items, noise can be critical in determining error patterns, as encoding more items might cause higher noise for each individual item (Chunharas et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chunharas et al., 2022.

claim: The modularity structure in the brain is thought to be advantageous for fast adaptation to changing environments.
source: The modularity structure in the brain is thought to be advantageous for fast adaptation to changing environments (Simon, 1995; Cole et al., 2013; Frankland and Greene, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Simon, 1995; Cole et al., 2013; Frankland and Greene, 2020.

claim: Recurrent neural networks trained for multiple cognitive tasks form clustered neural activities and modular dynamic motifs to repurpose shared functions for flexible computation.
source: Recent works showed that recurrent neural networks trained for multiple cognitive tasks form clustered neural activities and modular dynamic motifs to repurpose shared functions for flexible computation (Yang et al., 2019; Driscoll et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yang et al., 2019; Driscoll et al., 2022.

claim: An fMRI study showed that shared representation across distinct visual stimuli emerges during the delay period.
source: Resonant with these computational findings, an fMRI study showed that shared representation across distinct visual stimuli emerges during the delay period (Kwak and Curtis, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kwak and Curtis, 2022.

claim: A memory module with ring geometry can be repurposed for various visual stimuli such as motion, spatial location, and color.
source: Although our work focuses on a single task, it highlights the necessity of having dedicated sensory and memory modules, and a memory module with ring geometry can be repurposed for various visual stimuli such as motion, spatial location, and color.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the model architecture.

claim: The flexible working memory model proposes connections between multiple sensory modules and a control module.
source: It is reminiscent of the flexible working memory model, which proposes connections between multiple sensory modules and a control module (Bouchacourt and Buschman, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Bouchacourt and Buschman, 2019.

claim: Unlike the flexible working memory model that loses memory without sensory-control interactions, the memory module in the current work can independently maintain memory.
source: However, a key distinction lies in the role of the control module. Unlike the flexible working memory model that loses memory without sensory-control interactions, our work suggests that the memory module can independently maintain memory, while interaction with the sensory module continuously shapes the internal representation, potentially consolidating prior beliefs regarding natural statistics.
evidence: This is a comparison between the current model and the flexible working memory model.
